'''Clone shadow troopers''' were an elite cadre of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], devised by [[Director of Republic Intelligence|Director]] [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard]] of [[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Since the numbers of the [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|Advanced Recon Commandos]] were dwindling, Isard created the shadow [[Troop/Legends|troopers]] as a reconnaissance unit, who, with the benefit of greatly modified and expensive [[Armor/Legends|armor]], could operate covertly and undercover. Using [[Magnetic seal/Legends|magseals]] installed in their armor, shadow troopers could attach plates to themselves that could pass them off as [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] belonging to certain factions. With that advantage, they could infiltrate facilities and gather intelligence with ease.

During the late stages of the war, the role of the shadow trooper expanded, with some performing [[Sniper/Legends|sniper]] duties, while others would be used on the battlefield. Though their [[Jammer/Legends|jamming systems]] would prevent them from working alongside standard troopers, shadow troopers were occasionally dispatched before large-scale invasions to install jamming devices in key [[City/Legends|cities]], which would allow their comrades to infiltrate their targets with stealth and efficiency. Shadow troopers saw later use in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as guards to both facilities and individuals. In particular, [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitor]] [[Valin Draco]] enlisted a group of the troopers for his expedition to the [[Almas Academy]]. The shadow troopers would later become the model on which [[Storm commando/Legends|storm commandos]] and [[Shadow stormtrooper/Legends|shadow stormtroopers]] were based.

==History==
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Director of Republic Intelligence|Director]] [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard]] of [[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]] developed the shadow [[Troop/Legends|trooper]] division, which was created to serve as a reconnaissance tool. Their formation was designed to combat the dwindling numbers of [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|Advanced Recon Commandos]], but they could operate in a far more covert manner than that of the commandos. The shadow troopers were given highly modified and highly expensive [[Armor/Legends|armor]] that suited their roles better than the standard fatigues.<ref name="db" />

[[File:UtapauShadowTrooperCardArt.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A shadow trooper in action]]
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], when [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] was located on [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]], shadow troopers were called in to infiltrate six of the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] sinkhole [[City/Legends|cities]] and place [[Jammer/Legends|jammers]] that would allow<ref name="db" /> [[Jedi General/Legends|General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and the [[7th Sky Corps/Legends|7th Sky Corps]] to [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|invade]] the planet without notice. As a result, Grievous was killed, and Utapau was placed under [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] control.<ref name="rots">{{Film|III}}</ref><ref name="bfII">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>

In the aftermath of the Clone Wars, [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], now [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] following his [[Declaration of a New Order]], established a secret storehouse on Utapau and assigned the shadow troopers to guard it. While the rest of the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]] received an upgrade from the [[Phase II clone trooper armor/Legends|Phase II clone trooper armor]] to [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|stormtrooper armor]], shadow troopers retained their original appearance under the new regime, as a grim reminder of Palpatine's ascension. The phrase "[[Emperor's black bones]]" was said to have originated from someone who set eyes upon members of the cadre during Palpatine's reign.<ref name="eotj" />

[[File:Shale attack.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Clone shadow troopers with Imperial Captain Shale during the Atoan insurgency]]
In 19 BBY, Palpatine sent his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], to the [[Ghost Nebula/Legends|Ghost Nebula]] to find an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]], under the command of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Garoche Tarkin]], which had gone missing. Landing on the planet [[Atoa/Legends|Atoa]], Darth Vader and his [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] troopers [[Battle of Atoa|engaged]] the [[Atoan]] [[Soldier/Legends|forces]]. During the fighting, shadow troopers under the command of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Shale (human)|Shale]] were able to launch a sneak attack on the Atoans allowing the Imperial forces to defeat them.<ref name="SWDVLC1">[[Darth Vader and the Lost Command 1|''Darth Vader and the Lost Command'' 1]]</ref>

[[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitor]] [[Valin Draco]] enlisted the shadow troopers for his own cause, reasoning that if they were good enough to guard Palpatine's storehouses, they were good enough to guard him.<ref name="eotj" /> In circa [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''Echoes of the Jedi'' states that the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vhiin Thorla]] traveled to the Almas Academy two years after the declaration of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], which is dated to 19 BBY by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. This thus indicates that ''Echoes of the Jedi'' is set in circa 17 BBY.</ref> he took a small detachment of the troops to the [[Almas Academy]], where he searched for [[Darth Rivan's holocron]]. Within the academy, he and his guard were [[Mission to Almas|confronted]] and defeated by a group of [[Alderaanian Resistance]] agents working for the fugitive [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Denia]].<ref name="eotj" />

The success of Isard's shadow troopers would breed several variants in the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], in particular the [[Storm commando/Legends|storm commandos]] and the [[Shadow stormtrooper/Legends|shadow stormtroopers]], which were used by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] agent [[Cronal|Blackhole]].<ref name="db" />

==Equipment==
[[File:Clone_shadow_trooper_TCWCG.jpg|thumb|left|120px|A shadow trooper]]
Shadow trooper armor was based on standard Phase II [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] trooper armor, although it featured several strategically placed [[Magnetic seal/Legends|magseals]]. The magseals allowed for the placement of cosmetic plates that could alter each individual trooper's appearance, with different plates giving them the appearance of a [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]] or [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]], or other miscellaneous factions. While the plates could disguise the wearer's [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] signature and project the image of something other than a [[Human/Legends|Human]], they were primarily for appearances only.<ref name="db" />

The plates could also alter the walk of a [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]], disguising the "clone gait" that was familiar to some. A jaw switch was installed in the armor, in case a shadow trooper's identity was discovered. Activating the switch would disengage all magseals and allow the trooper to regain full use of his Phase II armor. As a further modification, the Phase II armor was covered with a sensor reflective material, which absorbed active scans. It was also protected from passive scans by [[thermal damper]]s and electro-magnetic hardening.<ref name="db" /> The visor of the helmet gave off a red glow, which, in conjunction with their dark appearance, was considered intimidating by some.<ref name="eotj" /> Some shadow troopers would wear [[Kama/Legends|''kamas'']] and [[Pauldron/Legends|pauldrons]].<ref name="rs.comII">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection|pack=Shadow Troopers (Jedi-Con 2008 Exclusive)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TACJCshadow.asp}}</ref>

Omni-directional jammers further enhanced the shadow trooper's invisibility, although with such devices in operation, they usually could not operate in close proximity with standard clone troopers, whose helmet systems would suffer the effects of the jamming. Instead of wielding the standard [[DC-15S/Legends|DC-15S]], shadow troopers were equipped with the [[DC-19 "Stealth" carbine]], which featured a sound suppressor, so the troopers could operate in relative silence. An optional function, which allowed the [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] to fire bolts invisible to the regular visual [[Spectrum/Legends|spectrum]], was favored by shadow trooper [[Sniper/Legends|snipers]]. The invisible bolts, however, were highly expensive, had to be reloaded after ten shots, and as a result of their usage, the DC-19s had to be cooled down afterwards to prevent damage to the weapon's dampeners. [[Vibrodagger/Legends|Vibrodaggers]] rounded out the shadow trooper armory.<ref name="db" /> In addition to their standard kit, troopers could use [[DC-15A blaster rifle/Legends|DC-15A blaster rifles]]<ref name="rs.com">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (toy line)|pack=Utapau Shadow Trooper (Super Articulation!)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/rots05shadowtrooper.asp}}</ref> and [[Scout trooper blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]] commonly utilized by [[Scout trooper/Legends|scout troopers]].<ref name="rs.comII" />

Although the distinctive standard [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|Republic gunship]] was not well suited for shadow troopers' generally low operational numbers and need for stealth, modified [[shadow trooper gunship]]s, equipped with highly advanced sensor-jamming packages and specialized sensor-refractive armor plating, were employed in cases where an entire [[Squad/Legends|squad]] was to be inserted behind enemy lines.<ref name="rs.comIII">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Titanium Series|pack=Shadow Trooper Gunship|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/SW08TSgunshipshadow.asp}}</ref>

==Application==
Used primarily for reconnaissance, shadow troopers would operate alone, in pairs, or, less commonly, in squads.<ref name="rs.comIII" /> While still in their armor, they would work undercover, posing as [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] or other mercenaries, which allowed them to discreetly enter and leave locations and adequately collect valuable intelligence. They were aided in their efforts by their effectively sensor-proof suits of armor. Due to the high-tech jamming equipment built into their armor, shadow troopers, for the most part, did not operate alongside standard clones, for fear of disrupting their comrades helmet systems.<ref name="db" />

Some shadow troopers operated as snipers, using the "invisible bolt" feature of the DC-19 carbine to great effect. In some situations, such as the one on Utapau in the waning days of the Clone Wars, shadow troopers were inserted to ensure the successful entry of a much larger invasion force.<ref name="db" /> During the reign of Emperor Palpatine, shadow troopers' roles would extend to protection, and they would be assigned to guard either installations or key personnel.<ref name="eotj" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Utapau_Shadow_Trooper.jpg|thumb|125px|The [[Hasbro]] shadow trooper action figure]]
The shadow trooper originated as a [[Hasbro]] action figure from the [[2005]] [[W:c:swmerchandise:Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']] line. The figure was a [[Wikipedia:Target Corporation|Target]] exclusive, and was labeled "[[W:c:swmerchandise:Utapau Shadow Trooper|Utapau shadow trooper]]."<ref name="rs.com" /> The backstory of the shadow troopers was elaborated on by [[Sam D. Garito]], writing under the alias of "Maso Tirag," through [[StarWars.com]]'s [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature "[[What's The Story?]]" In his writings, Garito made connections between the troopers and such elements from the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] as Armand Isard from [[Michael A. Stackpole]]'s ''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]'', and the Blackhole stormtroopers from [[Russ Manning]]'s ''[[Gambler's World]]''. The shadow troopers would later be used by [[Abel G. Peña]] and [[Jean-François Boivin]] in the [[Roleplaying game|role-playing]] adventure ''[[Echoes of the Jedi]]'' as non-player characters. In [[Star Wars Insider 100|''Star Wars Insider'' 100]], the shadow troopers were listed at number sixty-two in the [[The 100 Greatest Things About Star Wars... Ever!|''100 Greatest Things About Star Wars... Ever!'']] list. The article erroneously listed the ''[[Dusty Duck]]'', which came in at number seventy-one, to be the only "What's the Story?" entry to make the list. In 2008, more shadow trooper figures were produced by Hasbro, and were at first exclusively sold at Jedi-Con 2008, before being made available on [[StarWars.com]].<ref name="rs.comII" />

In the [[2011]] non-[[canon]]ical [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]'', a clone shadow trooper model can be built by obtaining all ten LEGO minikits in the "[[Blue Shadow Virus (episode)|Blue Shadow Virus]]" level. When this has been done, a clone shadow trooper can be purchased and used in the Free Play mode of the game. However, the "clone shadow trooper" is in reality an Imperial shadow stormtrooper.
